bio.en: Ray Cao is the global Head of Monetization Product Strategy & Operations at TikTok, where he has been for over four years, after spending six years at Google helping scale Google Shopping globally.
bio.zh: Ray Cao 是 TikTok 全球变现产品战略与运营负责人，已在公司四年有余，此前曾在 Google 工作六年，帮助 Google Shopping 在全球范围规模化。

summary.en: Ray pulls back the curtain on how TikTok operates, explaining its 'context, no control' culture that gives people full information and autonomy while expecting ownership. He discusses how TikTok fine-tunes its algorithm and product for different cultures, why it maintains a 'always day one' startup hunger, and what it takes to succeed as a creator or advertiser on the platform. The episode is a rare inside look at one of the most successful businesses in history.
summary.zh: Ray 揭开了 TikTok 的运作内幕，阐释了其“给背景、不给控制（context, no control）”的文化：在授予充分信息与自主权的同时，要求员工具备主人翁意识。他探讨了 TikTok 如何针对不同文化微调算法与产品、为何保持“永远第一天”的创业饥渴，以及作为创作者或广告主在该平台取得成功的关键。本期是对史上最成功企业之一难得的内部透视。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: We rarely get a peek into what it's like to work at TikTok. What are some core principles or values or just how TikTok operates?
turns.zh: 外界对TikTok的工作环境知之甚少。TikTok的核心价值观或运营理念是什么？

turns.speaker: Ray Cao
turns.en: The number one thing is context, no control. That's the reason why we're always encouraging people to see themselves as a business owner.
turns.zh: 最重要的一点是赋予员工自主权，而非进行微观管理。这也是我们始终鼓励员工把自己视为企业主的原因。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: You give them all the information they need and then let them just do things without specific instructions.
turns.zh: 你只需为他们提供所需的信息，然后让他们在没有具体指令的情况下自主开展工作。

turns.speaker: Ray Cao
turns.en: How do you actually solve the puzzle by connecting all the dots together? Just like how I see some of my friends, their kids playing Legos, if you don't really see the full picture, you won't be able to make the Lego as one thing at the end of the day. You have to see the other pieces.
turns.zh: 如何通过整合各方信息来破解难题？就好比我看到有些朋友让孩子玩乐高积木，如果不整体把握局面，最终拼不出完整的作品。你必须把各块积木的关联都理清。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: What else are important cultural values of TikTok, of how TikTok operates that everyone always has in mind when they're building?
turns.zh: 在TikTok的运营中，还有哪些重要的文化价值观是每个开发者在产品开发时都需要牢记的？

turns.speaker: Ray Cao
turns.en: We always have this mentality we are a startup, we're a young company, we're always hungry for growth. And a very wacky way is like, "How can I run my second half of my marathon faster than the first half?"
turns.zh: 我们始终秉持初创企业的思维模式，视自己为一家年轻且渴望成长的公司。其中一个颇具创意的策略是：“如何让马拉松后半程的速度比前半程更快？”

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: It's my pleasure. I wanted to start with a little bit about your time before TikTok, which was at Google and comparing that to TikTok. So, you're at Google for six years, I believe. Now you're at TikTok. I'm curious on what stood out to you about the cultural differences between how Google operates and TikTok operates.
turns.zh: 我也很荣幸。能邀请您来分享TikTok的工作模式、产品研发思路，以及如何在TikTok上成功开展业务和投放广告，我感到非常兴奋。所以我有许多问题想请教您。比如，您在谷歌工作的六年经历与TikTok的文化差异，尤其是在产品创新和市场运营方面的不同之处。

turns.speaker: Ray Cao
turns.en: Three major things, I would say. Number one is really how these two company thinking about innovation. So, I think Google has a very strong philosophy of we're engineering lab and that there's a lot of technology-driven, and a lot of pieces. They are not necessarily always trying to, I would say, cope with the market even, right? However, I think at the TikTok, I think besides the technology part, we do have a very keen, I would say, appetite to really understand what the markets really want and also how can we really service our clients in a better way and the clients here is not necessarily only for advertisers including our user and also creator altogether. So that's one of the things I think it's very different in terms of TikTok way of work. It's very customer-centric in a way, and again, the customer here is not necessarily only for the business partner but also for our regular user and creators on the platform. (00:06:39): And the second one is really thinking about how we take approach on product development. So a lot of times that we take a very rigid approach in terms of product development and oftentimes you see us that experimenting a lot of different things all the same time. And also we do have a lot of engineering and [inaudible 00:07:04] project in the backend to really understand how can we optimize better for the platform. So a lot of time, these are the things that I think TikTok is doing really, really well. (00:07:14): The last piece I have to say is the approach for global prioritization. A lot of times that you see a US-born company go global and oftentimes still they are really rooted with the US market and there's nothing wrong with it to be honest, because this is the biggest market for them as I would say for East-born company. I think a lot of times that we can take approach with truly how do we think about globalization and for example, we launched a lot of product not necessarily first in North America. We launched it in South Asia for example, for our shopping, really very big initiative internally for shopping and we launched our really creator fund here in North America. We launched our gaming approach, really serviced our EUI gaming advertisers. Really, really strong over there. So there are a lot of different approach in terms of how do we prioritize our go-to-market and also product development. So that's the part I feel like we're very unique in the market or unique to some of that was the tech company born in the US.
turns.zh: 我认为有三个关键点：首先，谷歌和TikTok在创新理念上存在显著差异。谷歌奉行工程实验室的理念，注重技术驱动和模块化设计，往往不急于迎合市场需求。而TikTok则更关注市场需求，致力于为用户、广告主和创作者提供更优质的服务。其次，TikTok在产品开发策略上更以用户为中心，重视市场反馈，持续进行多样化实验，并通过后台工程项目优化平台体验。最后，TikTok在全球化布局上采取差异化策略。许多美国出生的科技公司在国际化进程中往往深受美国市场影响，但TikTok更强调本土化创新，例如先在南亚推出购物功能，再引入北美创作者基金等举措，充分发挥本土优势。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: It reminds me there's this piece by this smart guy, Eugene Wei who wrote a few things about TikTok over the years and just why it's been so successful and one of his really big points is that TikTok can work really well in other markets 'cause it's basically... you don't need to know a ton about the market because it's this algorithm that figures out what people in each market want. Is there anything along those lines you've seen that just has been really fundamental to it working so well in many different markets?
turns.zh: 这让我想起了一位聪明人尤金·韦（Eugene Wei）的文章。多年来，他写过几篇关于TikTok的文章，深入剖析了它为何能如此成功。其中一个核心观点是，TikTok在其他市场也能运作得非常好，因为它基本上……你不需要对市场有太多的了解，因为算法会自动识别每个市场用户的需求。你们有没有看到过类似的例子？这些因素对TikTok在不同市场取得成功起到了至关重要的作用。

turns.speaker: Ray Cao
turns.en: The algorithm is definitely helping because it is basically the machine is doing a lot of heavy lifting. That's actually I think across the board on a technology company today. The difference is actually how much you are willing to take the heavy lifting over there in the market. By that I mean really sending your troops into the market, hiring your local talent, understanding the culture and really understanding the behavior from those users. I understand the machine can do things, but also at the same time that we need to actually get local talent to fine tune the machine. So there are a lot of conversations about how I would say technology is able to change our life, but I do think that at the end of the day, I do believe technology is a tool. (00:09:34): So if we do have a ambition to go global, you have to do one more thing is actually take your step into global. Rather than having the machine do the heavy lifting, you have to really understand in local culture. I had a fun background for my first job is to really doing go-to market research in the Southeast Asia area. I think there was only one thing opened my eyes after a year and a half in this career path is different market have totally different, I would say, culture and these market behaviors are actually coming out of this culture. One of the fun example I always been using was I was doing market research for one of the suppliers for toner and also these ink cartridges for Thailand as a go-to market research. One of the things is always concern to my, at that point, the client was they cannot figure out why their premium product cannot sell in Thailand and then we just figure out because the quality of their printing machine and also their ink cartridges are premium and the quality of the paper and everything is very good. (00:10:51): But when you actually do talk to those consumers in those market, the answer is very eye-opening. They literally told me at that time is I don't care. I don't care if your ink cartridges or your printer is at the premium quality, maybe the printer I can use, but I can use compatible ink cartridges or toner for that because my consumer won't care about your printing quality or the majority of my consumer won't care. So in that case you should not necessarily worried about if you are a premium product, it's actually more about how durable, how reliable you're able to print things and people can read. (00:11:30): So I think these are the insights I think a lot of times it will be neglected from some of clients or the manufacturers or even the owner of the business because they think that we want to serve this segmentation, but, however, this segmentation is that big in this area. So that's reason why the culture is really the key part from the market. If you don't understand the culture, you won't be able to understand the behavior over there. It's more about that, I think, when we say about globalization or take the product go to market in a global scheme or even build it apart, you have to get your hands dirty and to really understand the local culture so that you can understand local behavior.
turns.zh:
算法确实带来了帮助，因为它基本上承担了大量繁重的工作。这实际上是我认为当今科技公司普遍面临的挑战。关键在于，你愿意在当地市场投入多少精力。我的意思是，真正将团队派往市场，招聘本地人才，理解当地文化，深入了解用户行为。当然，机器可以完成某些任务，但我们也需要本地人才来对其进行微调。关于科技如何改变生活的讨论很多，但我认为归根结底，科技只是一种工具。

（00:09:34）：如果我们有全球化雄心，就必须亲自踏入全球市场。别指望机器来承担繁重任务，而是要深入理解当地文化。我最初的职位是东南亚地区的市场调研员，经过一年半的历练，我深刻认识到不同市场的文化差异巨大。比如，我曾为一家泰国墨盒和打印机供应商做市场调研。客户困惑为何高端产品在泰国滞销，而我们分析后发现问题出在打印机和墨盒的超高品质标准，用户更青睐兼容墨盒或低价产品。

（00:10:51）：深入用户调研后发现，他们不在乎产品质量，宁愿使用低价耗材。关键在于产品耐用性和可靠性，而非高标准。这种文化差异在全球市场普遍存在，企业常忽视本地化的重要性。

（00:11:30）：文化是市场成功的核心。若不理解当地行为模式，产品推广将徒劳无功。全球化战略需要亲力亲为，深入本土文化，调整产品以适应不同市场需求。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I love that advice, the way you described it, which I love also is that you kind of have to fine-tune the algorithm and the product to work in different cultures. Is there an example of how that was done with TikTok, like a tweak that had to be made or some kind of fine-tuning that happened for it to work in a different market?
turns.zh: 我很欣赏你的建议，你提到要根据不同文化微调算法和产品。能否举个TikTok的例子，说明在不同市场进行优化或微调的具体做法？

turns.speaker: Ray Cao
turns.en: Yeah. I think we did a lot of fine-tuning on our user product side to really think about content. So that's the number one thing going to be super different coming from each of the market and also from each of the culture. For example in Japan, how do you actually get more content that relevant for the culture? A lot of people may think, okay, are you guys only doing dancing or doing singing for Japan? The answer is not. It is actually more food on the TikTok side, like how do you actually introducing new food restaurant or new recipes and also sometimes that you're introducing a new technology. I would say 3C like consumer electronics product over there. So these are the content get really popular sometimes in Southeast Asia or even Japan area and versus in the US as everybody knows that we're starting from really lip-syncing at a very early stage but now really we're expanding to shopping behaviors and also a lot of people using us as a main platform to acquire new discovery for the product. (00:13:40): So these are the things I think different market definitely deserves and demand different kind of treatment and if you are able to do this a lot, you're able to find success over there.
turns.zh: 是的。我认为我们在用户产品方面做了很多微调，真正考虑了内容因素。所以这第一点在不同市场和不同文化中会有很大差异。比如在日本，如何获取更符合当地文化的优质内容？很多人可能会问，你们只为日本做跳舞或唱歌相关内容吗？答案并非如此。TikTok平台上其实有更多美食相关内容，比如如何推广新开的餐厅或新食谱，有时还会介绍新科技产品，比如3C类消费电子产品。这些内容有时在东南亚甚至日本地区会大受欢迎，而在美国则不然，因为众所周知，我们最初是从口型同步开始的，但现在已扩展到购物行为，许多用户将我们视为获取新产品发现的主要平台。（00:13:40）所以我认为不同市场的确需要不同的策略，如果能在这方面下足功夫，就能在当地取得成功。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That's really interesting because you could think it's just this algorithm that figures everything out for you, but I think what you're pointing out is you have to seed it with the right sorts of use cases that that culture is most excited about.
turns.zh: 这真的很有趣，因为你可能会认为算法会自动处理一切，但我认为你所强调的是必须用正确的用例来引导文化热点。

turns.speaker: Ray Cao
turns.en: Another good example will be creative, so it's a very good example how human can work with technology together. We have a ton of creatives and we have a ton of content so, of course, we use machine to label those content use metadata to analyze those content. However, a lot of times you can find that when we're really thinking about how creative can help advertisers? Humans actually make a more interesting or more, I would say, influencing decisions over there. For some of the verticals we can say that, "Oh, you know what, maybe we can try a coupon image with a new product like a sticker on the top?" This maybe actually work better compared to some of the price promotion even. So a lot of things really depends on how do you actually interpreting the numbers and interpreting the data points but also at the same time your business acumen is going to be very important here to make a judgmental call for some of the situation like that. I think we're still rely a lot on both machine and also our own experts to analyzing those trends and give it the recommendations.
turns.zh: 另一个很好的例子是创意内容，这很好地展示了人类如何与技术协同工作。我们有大量创意团队和内容资源，当然会用机器标注这些内容，利用元数据进行分析。但很多时候你会发现，当我们真正思考创意如何帮助广告主时，人类实际上会做出更有趣或更有影响力的决策。对于某些垂直领域，我们可能会说：“哦，也许我们可以尝试在新产品上加一个优惠券图片，再加上顶部的贴纸？”这可能比某些价格促销效果更好。所以很多事情都取决于如何解读数据和洞察趋势，同时商业敏锐度在某些情况下也至关重要。我认为我们仍然高度依赖机器和专家来分析趋势并提供建议。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Awesome. Okay, so there's a few threads I'm going to follow later. You talked about the product development process, so I'm going to want to spend time there, also about how to be successful in TikTok both as a creator also as a business, I'm excited to hear your advice there. But I want to spend a little more time first on just what it's like to work within TikTok and the culture of TikTok. What are some core principles or values or just how TikTok operates if you had to identify, here's the ways that we all think about what we want to do and the most important to your day-to-day work, what words and concepts come to mind?
turns.zh: 太棒了。好的，我稍后会深入探讨几个方面。你提到了产品开发流程，我想花时间了解一下。还有如何在TikTok上取得成功，无论是作为创作者还是商业伙伴，我很期待听听你的建议。但首先我想多花点时间了解在TikTok工作的情况以及TikTok的文化。如果你能总结一下，哪些核心原则或价值观，或者TikTok的运作方式，对我们的日常工作最为重要，你能想到哪些词汇和概念？

turns.speaker: Ray Cao
turns.en: The number one thing resonating really, really well with me is context, no control. Oftentimes when we are looking around companies different sizes, we're looking at how to collaborate. Oftentimes we see the behavior that a lot of people just working on a smaller piece based off their job description. So hey, you're working on go-to-market and you're working on data analytics, and you're working on this book of business and commerce, and you're working on auto industry for example. A lot of times that these human-made silos is actually slowing things down because humans are not, or our talent, they're not supposed to be categorized into different basket. They may have their own majority responsibility for sure, but we don't want to cap them into this kind of a box we created. That's really why we're always encouraging people to think out of the box and think more and think themselves as a business owner rather than a piece of machine that keep the machine running. (00:16:49): Oftentimes that will say context, no control. That means you actually can go above and beyond to really think about your whole business problem as your own problem and your piece is maybe one part of it to solve the puzzle, but how do you actually solve the puzzle by connecting all the dots together, we're encouraging all the people to think like that way and by that I think we kind of mentally break out those walls. So encouraging our team members to do a little bit more thinking is very important. It's a little bit more thinking because the think part is very important. (00:17:23): And then, now in terms of getting things into behavior or changes or getting to action, then you need to really collaborate with other teams because we don't want to necessarily creating, hey, you're on other people's working group now you're actually stepping on other people's toes now. It is not the situation we're trying to encourage in, but where it's encouraging more is context, no control, think more about how you can change it and then we you do really actually take some actions, be active. You reach out to who's supposed to be the owner of that and then have a discussion so then you you're able to connecting the dots altogether. (00:18:00): So that's one thing I think it's very unique to our culture. I think it's very, very important for us to continue to grow at this speed because everybody have a, I would say, full visibility towards our full ownership to their mindset, how they can contribute.
turns.zh:
对我来说，最深刻的理念是"强调背景信息，放手让团队自主发挥"。很多时候，当我们观察不同规模的公司时，我们关注的是如何促进团队协作。但我们常常看到这样的现象：许多人只是根据自己的职位描述开展工作，比如你负责市场推广、数据分析、商业拓展，或者专注于汽车行业等领域。这种人为划分的部门壁垒实际上会拖慢进程，因为人才不应被简单归类到不同框架中。他们固然有主要职责，但我们不应将他们框在我们设定的条条框框里。这正是我们一直鼓励员工跳出固有思维、像企业主一样思考而非机器零件的原因。

（00:16:49）："强调背景信息，放手让团队自主发挥"。意思是，你可以突破常规，将整个商业难题视为自己的挑战，尽管你负责的模块只是解决拼图的一块，但如何通过整合各方资源破解难题才是关键。我们鼓励员工这样思考，这样就能打破思维壁垒。因此，激发团队的深度思考至关重要——思考本身就是核心。

（00:17:23）：在将想法转化为行动时，必须与其他团队紧密协作。我们不希望看到员工加入别人的工作组后互相扯皮。这不是我们提倡的模式。我们更强调在充分了解全局的基础上，主动思考如何变革现状，真正采取行动。主动找到负责人，共同探讨，最终实现各环节的无缝衔接。

（00:18:00）：这正是我们文化的独特之处。我认为保持这种思维方式对我们的快速发展至关重要，因为每个人都能清晰认识到自己对业务的全权负责，以及如何为公司创造价值。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And the key there is context implying you give them all the information they need and then let them just do things without giving them specific instructions, "Hey, I need you to hit this goal, work on this project, launch this thing. Here is what we know, do the things you think are best, roughly." Right now, I know it's not just like anyone does anything, but I imagine that's kind of the implication there.
turns.zh: 这里关键在于"背景信息"，意味着你要为团队提供所需的全部信息，然后放手让他们自主行动，而不是下达具体指令："你需要达成这个目标、负责这个项目、推出这个产品。以下是我们掌握的信息，你可以灵活处理。"目前来看，这并非是随意放任，但我认为这正是其核心含义。

turns.speaker: Ray Cao
turns.en: Yeah, I think it's context, no control plus proactive thinking and reactive doing so you have to do more proactive thinking with these contexts. Now reactive doing means that you need to collaborate, but when everybody has this kind of mindset, the collaboration should be very smooth because people have the context altogether. The part that I see maybe some of the other company are facing challenges is actually there's too many IOs in between and you have people that are just protecting their own thing and working their own thing and then I'm delivering. But just like how I see some of my friends, their kids playing Legos, if you don't really see the full picture, you won't be able to make the Lego as a one thing at the end of the day. You have to see the other pieces. So that's the part I think it's really powerful and reasoning really, really well when we're really thinking about product development and also product go-to-market. So it's a pretty full cycle. People have to see this and then they have the context.
turns.zh: 是的，我认为这涉及到上下文、缺乏控制以及主动思考与被动行动之间的平衡。因此，在面对这些情境时，我们需要进行更多主动思考。所谓被动行动，意味着需要与他人合作，但当所有人都具备这种思维模式时，合作应该会非常顺畅，因为大家都能共享同样的背景信息。我认为其他公司可能面临的挑战在于，过多的中间环节导致人们只顾保护自己的利益，各自为政，最终导致交付受阻。就像我观察一些朋友带孩子玩乐高积木时发现，如果不通盘考虑，最终拼不出完整的作品。同样，在产品开发和市场推广过程中，主动思考和理性分析也至关重要。这是一个完整的闭环，人们必须先理解整体，再构建上下文。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I love this, and this has come up actually a few times recently when I was talking to the CTO of Netflix and also OpenAI. They're very similar in culture where it's give people a lot of autonomy and freedom and not a lot of do this, do this, do this. The key there is to hire very high quality people and very high caliber people because if not, then things won't work out too great. Is there anything along those lines that you can share just like yeah, the kinds of people you end up hiring and how you hire people that can work well in that environment?
turns.zh: 我很认同这种观点。最近在与Netflix和OpenAI的CTO交流时，我发现他们的文化非常相似——给予员工高度的自主权和自由，避免微观管理。关键在于要招聘高素质人才，否则一切都难以顺利开展。您能否谈谈如何招聘到能在这种环境中高效工作的优秀人才？

turns.speaker: Ray Cao
turns.en: I agree with you. So the caliber of these people is actually pretty important to support the structure I just talked about, and oftentimes I can see some people that with the quality of always curious. Curiosity is a very important quality when I'm actually talking to my interviewers because I want to see that they are naturally curious to new things. They want to learn more about the new things and don't really get stuck with their own things. That's one thing. And the other thing is the discipline because like I said, it is actually a double-edged sword in this case. So it could potentially introducing some of the chaotic situation in a company because everybody is thinking everything. The discipline here is actually how you are really following the guidance on reactive doing, be always thinking about how to collaborating, and the discipline here and also the rigorous approach here is also going to be very important. (00:21:07): One of the good example that is the ability to prioritize because I don't believe one thing is everybody can do everything. You have to prioritize properly so that you're able to push the right agenda. So I think that's more of the quality of the people we're looking for is... it is hard, don't get me wrong. It is really hard to say that we can find everyone like that, but we would love to believe that we can train our employees like that so that they're able to even do better in their longer-term career.
turns.zh: 我完全赞同。人才的素质对支撑我提到的结构至关重要。我常发现有些人天生充满好奇心。在面试时，好奇心是关键品质——我希望候选人能主动探索新事物，渴望学习而非固守既有思维。这是第一要素。第二是纪律性。正如我所说，纪律性在这里是把双刃剑——过度自由可能导致混乱。因此，培养主动协作的纪律性至关重要。（00:21:07）：优先级管理是优秀人才的典范特征。我认为并非所有人都具备全能能力，需要合理分配资源，推动核心任务。培养这种能力确实不易，但我们希望通过培训帮助员工在职业生涯中持续成长。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Essentially what you look for when you're hiring people is making sure they're always curious, they have high discipline, and that they prioritize well. Coming back to the cultural pieces of TikTok, so the main one you've shared so far is this idea of context, not control. What else are important cultural values of TikTok, of how TikTok operates that everyone always has in mind when they're building and new meetings, making decisions?
turns.zh: 基本上，在招聘人才时，我们要确保他们始终保持好奇心、具备高度的自律性，并能善于分配优先级。回到TikTok的文化核心部分，目前你们分享最多的理念是"以情境而非控制为导向"。那么，TikTok的其他重要文化价值观还有哪些？在团队建设和新会议中，人们做决策时始终铭记的核心理念是什么？

turns.speaker: Ray Cao
turns.en: Yeah, another internal thing that we always say is always day one, we want to make sure that we always have this mentality we are a startup. We are a young company. We're always hungry for growth. We don't want to fall into the trap that people may think, "Oh, you guys are very successful in the market and then you are not necessarily need to worry about your existence anymore." I think it is actually something we're trying to avoid. We always want to make sure that in our team members always think like, "Okay, if this is actually a new day for you, I know what other things that you always want to keep in your mind you want to do." And also to keep that spirit is very important. (00:22:42): A lot of times that I can see some of the mature company, they're not necessarily losing the edge of, I would say this competition or losing the edge of being innovative. I think it's more about some of the culture has been shifted because you have a lot of new employees that live in your culture. So not necessarily it's not going to be like the old days that the co-founder is sitting among you, but I do think this company has a very interesting behavior. I see there is I can talk to anyone at any time via our internal communication system. I can ping Shuo right now. I can ping the co-founder if I want to tomorrow. (00:23:24): We always keep this kind of mentality internal is that we're still a young company, we want to grow and you can feel free to talk to anyone. We don't have a limitation for that as long as you have a good opinion, I would love to hear from you. Is that creating some of the, I would say chaotic situation? It might be, but I do think that this keeps the company very energetic. People are willing to share, people are willing to engage. That's very important. (00:23:50): I want add one more thing. We just talked about, you asked me what is actually the uniqueness of TikTok versus the other company. It's very tied up to that is I have never seen a company, the engineering team and the product team and the sales team are so close. That's definitely one of aha moments I had because if you're thinking about if your engineer does not really know what the market wants and if your PM doesn't really know what is actually the client's feedback, they won't be able to get a right product in the market. They just won't be. And they won't even tell a good go-to-market story to advertisers or even to our users because they just don't know what the end users are thinking. (00:24:39): So I think it's a very secret sauce for us is that our sellers and our engineering team and our product team and also data scientist team, we're all collaborating really, really closely and that's very much, I would say a such big advantage for us compared to when a company becomes too big and nobody talks to each other. So I do hope that it is the thing that we're going to continue reinforce along the years where we'll continue to grow the company.
turns.zh: 是的，我们内部经常强调的理念是"始终保持第一天的新鲜感"。我们要确保团队始终保持创业心态，保持年轻公司的活力，不陷入"市场成功后便无需再担忧生存"的陷阱。这正是我们努力避免的。我们希望团队成员始终保持这样的心态："好吧，如果今天是新的一天，那我就知道自己需要关注什么、需要做什么。"保持这种精神至关重要。（00:22:42）：我注意到许多成熟公司会失去竞争优势或创新动力。这更多是由于新员工加入后文化变迁所致。虽然联合创始人已不再亲临现场，但公司仍保持着独特的行为模式。比如，我可以通过内部通讯系统随时与任何人沟通，现在就给硕发消息，明天想找联合创始人交流也完全没问题。（00:23:24）：我们内部始终秉持"我们仍是年轻公司，渴望成长"的理念，鼓励自由交流。只要观点有价值，我们都乐于倾听。这会带来一些混乱吗？或许会有，但这恰恰激发了团队活力。人们乐于分享、积极参与，这至关重要。（00:23:50）：我想补充一点。我们讨论了TikTok相较其他公司的独特之处。这与工程团队、产品团队和销售团队的高度协作密切相关。这让我深有感触——如果工程师不了解市场需求，产品经理不清楚用户反馈，产品就无法准确推向市场，甚至无法向广告主或用户讲好产品故事，因为他们根本不了解终端用户的真实想法。（00:24:39）：因此，我认为我们的秘诀在于销售团队、工程团队、产品团队和数据科学团队之间深度协作。这与公司规模过大、各部门互不沟通形成鲜明对比。我希望这种文化能在未来几年内不断深化，随公司发展而壮大。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: What does that actually look like? I imagine people hearing this are like, "Yeah, we're going to make sales and product and hinge very close." I imagine many people don't actually do this too well. How do you actually execute that? Is it they report to the same leader, they sit next to each other or I don't know, zoom next to each other? What actually makes that work?
turns.zh: 具体来说是怎样的呢？我能想象听到这话的人会说：“是啊，我们要让销售和产品紧密协作。” 但我猜很多人做得并不理想。具体该怎么做呢？是让他们向同一位领导汇报？还是让他们坐在一起开会？或者用视频会议的方式？到底怎样才能真正实现协作？

turns.speaker: Ray Cao
turns.en: Yeah, I think a couple of things. Number one is a structure. Everything has to go at a structure. So we do have a meeting structure that we called it... it used to be by month and now it's actually a quarterly level. We get everybody together, engineering leader, product leader, and also not necessarily only the leader level. Some of the team members, we're joining the force together to have a big meeting. That meeting is 180 people-ish. It's crazy to have a meeting at that size, especially that there are different kind of functionality there. But one thing we keep really well is actually we are using a reading format of meeting. So it's a doc reading. We just read in comments and understanding the context again. It is the doc, bring everybody together, and then we discuss the things that we want to make a decision with or the things that we feel is a blocker or things that we need to celebrate. (00:26:24): So that meeting structure keep everybody together and consensus, again, not necessarily only for the top leaders. It's normal for the engineering leader and product leader and sales leader at the company level, they talk to each other, but we made that happen for their core team members. And the very beginning of my time here, that was literally getting to the IC level. So it is pretty eye-opening for me to join that meeting first time because I was get so used to their level of different meetings at Google, but here it's like, okay, everybody read one documentation and then you just understand what are people talking about or thinking about. It is intentional. But I do think that that structure is a very big secret sauce, I would say, not necessarily we invented it, right? We also learned from the other companies. So it is actually one of the things that we actually deployed pretty well today here to keep that structure running. (00:27:22): And the other thing is really feed those, I would say, first-hand market information to our PMs and RDs. That means we took them out with us. We're just inviting them together to join the force together to meet the clients and a lot of the company, if you want to meet APMs, if you want to meet the engineering leaders, it's literally once a year maybe, and also if you're investing a ton with some of the platforms. For us, I think it's always on to junior PMs, senior PMs and engineering leaders. We invited them together to these immersion trips recorded to really get face time with our clients, to really feel the heat. They are actually really facing a challenge by using our own product. (00:28:07): So that kind of, I would say, the aha moment is bringing a lot of, I would say, insights to them and also get them to feel the heat of the pains the sellers may feel. So that worked really well, too. I think oftentimes it is a battle. It is not necessarily the general, you have to stay in the back, you sometimes have to go to the front, but we just make sure that the general go to the front quite often in our company to do that.
turns.zh: 嗯，我觉得关键有几点：首先是建立一个结构化流程。一切都必须围绕结构来开展。我们现在有一个会议机制，之前是按月开，现在改成了季度汇报。每次会议汇集了工程、产品和销售负责人，以及团队成员。我们会让核心团队成员一起参与，规模通常有180人左右。这种大规模会议很疯狂，毕竟涉及不同部门的功能协作。但关键是我们采用了文档阅读的会议模式。每次会议先通读文档，理解上下文，再讨论需要决策的事项、阻碍进展的问题或值得庆祝的成果。（00:26:24）这种会议结构能让大家保持一致意见，不只是高层领导。工程、产品和销售负责人也会经常沟通，但我们把这种机制延伸到了核心团队成员层面。刚来这里的时候，我参加了IC层级的会议，真是大开眼界。我在谷歌习惯了不同层级的会议，但这里完全不同。大家一起阅读一份文档，就能理解彼此的想法。这是刻意设计的。我认为这种结构是关键的成功秘诀，虽然不是我们原创的，但确实借鉴了其他公司的经验。（00:27:22）另外，我们会让产品经理和研发人员直接接触一手市场信息。比如带他们参加客户会议，了解公司的不同部门。通常高管一年才见一次APM或工程负责人，如果他们深度参与某个平台开发，可能一年见一次。而我们会定期让初级PM、高级PM和工程负责人一起参加沉浸式访问，真正与客户面对面交流，感受市场压力。他们亲自使用我们的产品，切实感受到挑战的紧迫性。这种做法效果显著。很多时候这是一场斗争，不能总是躲在后方，有时必须冲到前线，但我们公司确保高层能经常亲自参与，推动变革。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I love that concept of having them feel the heat. An interesting trend I've noticed is there's a lot of Amazon influence on the way you all operate. It's always day one idea. There's the memo culture you just described. Any idea where that comes from? Is there like a senior Amazon person that came in and helped influence those sorts of things? Is it just hey, Amazon's killing in there? I've noticed interestingly, Amazon has influenced the most companies in all of their ways of working, so it's not a surprise. I'm just curious if there's anything else there that's interesting.
turns.zh: 我很欣赏让员工感受到紧迫感的理念。我注意到一个有趣的趋势——你们所有人的运营方式都深受亚马逊的影响。这始终是一种"第一天"的思维模式。您刚才提到的备忘录文化，这种文化的来源是什么？是否有亚马逊的高管曾介入并影响过这些做法？还是说大家只是觉得亚马逊在这些方面做得很出色？我发现亚马逊对其他公司的工作方式影响最深，这并不令人意外。我很好奇是否还有其他值得关注的细节。

turns.speaker: Ray Cao
turns.en: I think we have the benefits to standing on the shoulder of all the giants. So we learned definitely always there when the culture that Amazon was always championing, I think we learned from them. So this is something that we, I would say, always trying to listen and trying to learn from industry. The dark fashion is also learned from Amazon, so we kind of studied, oh, this is maybe one of the best practices we can employ here, how we deploy here. So we tried it, not even mentioned we have the OKR system, so it is actually a very good learning from our early stage from Google. So all these, I think definitely we do have some of the, I would say, benefits being the newcomer to the market and then learn a lot of the best practices coming from our industry peers and really deployed here hopefully successfully. (00:29:53): And some of the things that we just tweaked. So for example our culture always day one is definitely very similar to Amazon, but the implementation of that could be different. And also the context, no control piece is, I believe other companies may have the similar idea, but for us I think we just really need to implement it in a way that's going to be fitting to us. I happened to listen to your podcast with the Airbnb co-founder the other day. He also mentioned that how he break out the IOs. I think it is very similar approach among industry right now trying to really make sure the team is able to talk to each other because I think a quote from him, "If your PM doesn't know how to sell the product they're creating, you won't be able to do your job better." So this is literally how we're thinking about it, too, in a lot of way.
turns.zh: 我认为我们确实能站在巨人的肩膀上受益。因此，我们从亚马逊始终倡导的文化中汲取了经验，这一点显而易见。例如，我们学习了OKR系统，这实际上是从谷歌早期阶段借鉴而来的。所有这些经验都让我们受益匪浅，作为市场新秀，我们能从行业同行那里借鉴最佳实践，并成功应用于自身业务中。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I know that you all move very fast and I want to actually talk about that next. And with that it feels like your value should be, it's always the first half of the day instead of it's always day one. It's always the morning of the first day.
turns.zh: 我知道你们的行动速度非常快，接下来我想深入探讨这一点。从这个角度来看，价值不应停留在"第一天"，而应转变为"每天清晨"。

turns.speaker: Ray Cao
turns.en: I think the value, if I put it in a very reactive way is, "How can I run my second half of my marathon faster than the first half?" So that's how I think about it and how do we really continue pushing for it.
turns.zh: 我认为从更积极的角度来看，关键在于"如何让下半场跑得比上半场更快？"这就是我们的思考方式，也是我们持续推进的动力。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Wow, that sounds very hard and painful, but I like that metaphor. Okay, so let's talk about how you set up the product org to move as fast as you move. I think there's this idea of just running fast. I don't know if that's a phrase you use, but just how is the product org set up, especially different from other teams that you've seen that allows it to move as quickly as you move and innovate as often as you all innovate?
turns.zh: 哇，这听起来既艰难又痛苦，但我很欣赏这种比喻。好的，让我们谈谈如何构建产品团队，使其像你们一样行动迅速。我认为核心理念就是"快速前行"。不知道你们是否有特定的术语，但产品团队是如何组织的，与其他团队相比有何不同？正是这些差异让你们能如此高效创新。

turns.speaker: Ray Cao
turns.en: Our product teams are setting, I would say, very importantly is global. So we want to actually, like I said, the number one step is if we really want to do global business, we have to go global. So we set up teams really across the board in the global locations to really acquire global talent who knows the market and who knows the competition, too. So we're able to really getting the, let's say jumpstart, in the local market. So for example, we have the majority of the engineer and also PMs currently located in the west coast of North America, so Los Angeles and also San Jose. These are the key hubs we have for our tech folks and also for North America wise we do have our majority of the go-to-market leads sitting in New York to get closer with our seller and also with our clients at the same time. (00:32:27): Also, it is not necessarily only for North America. Like I said, we heavily invested in Southeast Asia, so you can see that a lot of our engineering and also PM resources are deployed over there in Singapore to enable them to get closer to our clients over there as well. So really deploy your resources globally and also focusing on the key markets you want to penetrate. That's the commitment. I think we're doing pretty good in this case. And the second one is to really, again, I think the PMs and the product team of settings are oftentimes I would say because we're growing so fast, oftentimes we have to do a lot of minor team adjustment to catering for that. So it is very usual or common for teams to do a little bit of work on an annual basis or even on a two years or three year cycle. The stability is important, don't get me wrong, but I do think that as a faster growing company, we need to consistently to reiterate not only the product but also our teams. (00:33:33): So how can we do reiteration on the PM side, on the go-to-market side, it is actually something that I have seen this company doing really, really well. Not necessarily we're bonding to one team structure. We're actually bonding to the market need and we're bounding to the growth we're looking for. So we're not afraid to break our seams. And actually I literally break out my team last year to make sure that my team having more go-to-market mindset to actually embedded them with seller directly. So these are the things that very, I would say conventional to a size of this company, but I do think that's necessary and also that's a good mentality for the team to really run faster with this kind of a rigid approach. So yeah, these are the two things I think very unique to us, I think could also be continuously helping us in the next phase of the growth.
turns.zh: 我们的产品团队正在进行布局，我想说，这一点非常重要——全球化布局。正如我之前所说，如果我们真心想开展全球业务，首要步骤就是要实现全球化。因此，我们在全球各地组建了团队，专门招募既了解市场又熟悉竞争环境的全球化人才。这样一来，我们就能在当地市场迅速打开局面。例如，目前我们大部分工程师和产品经理都位于北美西海岸的洛杉矶和圣何塞。这些是我们技术团队的核心枢纽，而在北美市场方面，我们的大多数市场拓展负责人则驻守纽约，以便与销售团队和客户保持密切联系。（00:32:27）当然，这不仅限于北美地区。正如我之前提到的，我们在东南亚也进行了大力投入。可以看到，我们在新加坡部署了大量工程和产品资源，以便更贴近当地客户。总之，要在全球范围内合理配置资源，并聚焦于关键的目标市场。这就是我们的承诺。在这方面，我认为我们做得相当不错。第二点是关于产品团队和产品经理的设置。正如我所说，由于我们发展迅速，团队调整不可避免。每年、每两年甚至每三年对团队进行微调是常见的。稳定性固然重要，但作为一家快速发展的公司，我们需要不断迭代产品和团队。（00:33:33）那么如何在产品经理和市场拓展团队中进行迭代呢？这正是我们公司做得非常出色的地方。我们不拘泥于单一的团队结构，而是根据市场需求和发展目标灵活调整。我们从不畏惧打破常规。去年，我甚至将团队进行重组，让他们更深入地融入市场，直接与销售团队合作。这些做法在我们这种规模的公司中或许算不上特别，但我认为这确实必要，也是保持团队快速发展的正确思路。所以，这两点是我们独具特色的优势，也将持续助力我们下一阶段的增长。

turns.speaker: Ray Cao
turns.en: Yeah, when I joined the company, there were only two people on the go-to-market side.
turns.zh: 是的，我加入公司时，市场团队只有两个人。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: For the advertising business.

turns.speaker: Ray Cao
turns.en: There are only two people and by that time the US and plus, I would say, Europe business together, we're having less than 80 people, but the business needs to grow and we need to hire really fast. The first mistake I made was... By the way, the goal is to hiring 100 people in a six month to support the go-to-market. That is the speed we're into. So that is early 2020 to middle of 2020. So within six months I need to hire, I would say, 100 people to supporting the global go-to-market structure and build everything. Then the first mistake I made just at the right point because we're trying to grow too fast and sometimes as a hiring manager I have to compromise the standard we're trying to hire. So that's the mistakes I think I made first and I think nobody should repeat that mistake is you need to always run for the quality rather than the quantity. So it's a easy mistake. You can fall into the trap because the business demands you to go faster. If you don't have the manpower, you won't be able to. (00:37:11): But I would say, believe me when I say this, this is a pain, right, when you have the wrong people on the team, it's not necessarily going to make you move faster, it's going to actually slow you down. So that's one of the biggest mistake I made for my first year when I created the team and not necessarily myself only. So also the managers reporting to me, they're facing the same pressure and then it's cascading down. So it's definitely the mistakes we made at early stage. (00:37:43): The second thing I can think about is really on the context, no control. It is not necessarily I'm born into, to be honest, because I was trained really like, "Hey, this is your box, finish your work here and then you're good." But the reason why I value that really the attitude more today is literally I failed at the very early stage of my time here because I was trying to creating that kind of a very black and white discipline for my team, "You can do this, you cannot do that." But technically speaking, that's literally slowing things down because a lot of times you can see that, "Hey, we're delivering our go-to-market strategy and we're good." But literally what you don't know is your goal is not to deliver the go-to-market strategy. Your goal is to land your go-to-market strategy with sales together. So if your job only is delivering, no, you're failed oftentimes because you're not really getting the market context, you're not even talking to your clients. So that was literally another mistake I think taught me how to really embrace the culture. Here is context, no control. (00:38:52): And the third piece, I think, it's also a mistake, really a hard moment for me as well is, for the past couple of years now, I've been managing a such big global organization, oftentimes even not myself, my managers, they don't have time to go detail and to go talk to the clients, which is very scary because again, if you don't know, you don't hear what is happening in the market, you won't know the details in the market, you won't be able to take the right movement or take the right approach to go to market or even give the feedback to the engineering team. (00:39:32): So it's very important that the leader at any level needs to be situational. You cannot always down to the wheat and you cannot really distance yourself from the reality. So you need to find the balance to really get engaged and also see yourself out there to getting, I would say, getting deeper into the problems, to identify the problems, and then you're able to perform even better. Because I don't believe one thing is you are the pure, I was the people manager. You cannot do that because when you do that, you're very, very at the very, I would say, position to really thinking about your career because you're losing your competitive edge from the other, I would say equivalent talents in the market.
turns.zh:
当时只有两人，再加上美国和欧洲的业务团队，我们总共不到80人，但业务需要扩展，我们急需快速招人。我的第一个错误就是……顺便说一下，我们的目标是在六个月内招聘100人来支持市场推广。这就是我们当时的速度安排——从2020年初到2020年中期。所以在六个月内，我需要招聘大约100人来支持全球市场推广架构并完成所有筹备工作。然后，第一个错误出现在关键节点，因为我们扩展速度太快，作为招聘经理，我不得不降低招聘标准。这是我认为最先犯的错误，任何人都不能重蹈覆辙——你必须始终追求质量而非数量。这是个容易犯的错误，你可能会陷入追赶业务进度的陷阱。如果没有足够的人力支持，你根本做不到。（00:37:11）但我要强调，团队里有不合适的人选真的很痛苦，这不仅不会加速进程，反而会拖慢进度。这是我第一年组建团队时最大的失误之一，不光是我自己，手下经理也面临同样的压力，问题就层层传递下去了。所以这些都是早期阶段犯的错误。（00:37:43）第二个教训在于缺乏上下文把控。说实话，这不是天生的问题，因为我接受的培训是：“做好本职工作，完成任务就行。”但如今我更重视团队的积极态度。早期我曾试图为团队建立黑白分明的纪律规则——“能做什么，不能做什么”。但从技术层面看，这其实是在拖后腿。比如我们以为市场推广策略实施得很顺利，但实际上目标不应该是执行策略，而是要让销售团队共同落地策略。如果只是一味执行，却不了解市场动态、没有与客户沟通，那就注定失败。这让我深刻领悟到文化融合的重要性。（00:38:52）第三个教训同样让我刻骨铭心——过去几年管理如此庞大的全球团队时，我自己和下属经理都忙于应付日常事务，根本无暇深入客户端。这很可怕，因为如果你不了解市场动态，就无法准确判断市场需求，也无法制定有效的市场策略，甚至无法给工程团队反馈。（00:39:32）所以各级领导必须保持灵活应变，不能拘泥于条条框框。既要深入问题核心，又要保持对现实的敏锐洞察，这样才能高效决策。正因如此，我现在更加重视与团队的深度协作，共同识别问题根源，从而提升整体绩效。
别以为自己很清高。我曾担任过人力资源经理。你可不能这么做，因为一旦你这么做了，你就相当于把自己置于一个非常不利的位置，无法真正为自己的职业生涯着想，因为你会失去相较于市场上其他同等水平人才的竞争优势。

Is there something that just doesn't stick with people that often leads to this is not the place for me?
turns.zh: 我喜欢这些故事。我喜欢讲述事情进展不顺的经历，所以很感激你能与我们分享。当有人在TikTok工作不顺、遭遇挫折、被解雇或主动离职时，除了能力不足之外，最常见的原因是什么？是否存在某种难以让人适应的文化，导致他们觉得"这里不适合我"？

turns.speaker: Ray Cao

So I definitely can see we're just talking about people being very curious and people are very, being nimble. They can be more successful here. At the same time, I think we have to admit one thing, join a start-up and join a rocket ship is a lifestyle. It is not necessarily a job you are working on from 9 to 5. So it is a different lifestyle and it is not built for everyone. So if you are not able to adjust your mentality towards some of the work that we are here to do and it's maybe not right fit for you. I'm not saying that that candidates is incapable. I think they could be capable in the other scenario for sure, but is the right fit? I think that is, I would say very much towards the situation or the company status in the market. (00:41:33): I can see a lot of people that they left and become very successful, too. So it is not necessarily that, "Oh, we think you're not good and then you're going to be not good for every single other company." That's not the case. (00:41:46): And one thing, and also this is my team culture I try to create is, I'm happy to say that when an employee reach out to me, say, "Hey Ray, I'm actually leaving the company," as long as they're telling me that they're going to a better place or a place that they can continue to grow their career, I'm happy for them because oftentimes my last question during my interview is, "What is actually your goal in the next three to five years?" And also I'd be really honest with them, say, "Hey, I don't think this is the job for you forever. Nobody going to work in this forever. If you can, great. But what is really your North Star?" I think that's the part that I would love to co-partner with you because I always believe one thing is it is not only about achieving the company goal, it's also achieving really the career goal or your employee's career goal together. (00:42:41): So I want to creating that culture here as well. So yeah, I think I'm doing so far so good. Most of my team members when they actually are moving on internally or externally, I'm able to say that, "Okay, that's a good choice. If I were you, I may probably do the same thing." It is actually a very good culture, I think, I would love to champion across.
turns.zh: 是的，我会尝试用不同的角度去思考这个问题。从我观察到的情况来看，人们在这里能更成功。关键在于保持好奇心和灵活性。这里确实更适合那些有上进心、善于学习的人。但同时我们必须承认，加入初创公司或快速发展的公司，本质上是一种生活方式，而不只是朝九晚五的工作。这种生活方式并非适合所有人。所以如果一个人无法适应我们这里特定的工作环境，可能就不太适合这里。我不是说这些候选人能力不足——他们在其他环境下或许能大放异彩，但这里是否真的合适？我认为这很大程度上取决于公司在市场中的地位和现状。（00:41:33）我也见过很多离职后取得巨大成功的人。所以问题不在于“我们认为你不够优秀，然后你就注定在其他公司也做不好”。事实并非如此。（00:41:46）还有一点，也是我努力营造的团队文化：当员工主动找我说“雷，我要离开公司了”，只要他们告诉我会去一个更好的平台、能继续成长的地方，我都会为他们感到高兴。因为我在面试时最后一个问题通常是：“未来三到五年你的目标是什么？” 我也会坦诚地说：“嘿，我觉得这份工作不适合你永远做下去。没人能永远在这里工作。如果你能适应，那很好。但你的北极星目标是什么？” 我认为这部分我很乐意与你共同探讨，因为我始终相信，成功不仅关乎达成公司目标，更在于与员工共同实现职业目标。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: On that first point, I'm also a huge advocate of just, "You'll be successful if you work very hard." I know there's a bit of a backlash at working along and thinking too much about work-life balance. And I feel like it's actually really important to work a lot and work long hours often to be successful, especially at a company that's going through this 'cause that's not going to last forever.
turns.zh: 关于第一个观点，我也非常赞同“只要你足够努力就能成功”的说法。我知道有些人对加班和平衡工作与生活有抵触情绪。但我认为多工作、长时间工作对成功至关重要，尤其是在这样快速发展的公司里，因为这种状态不会永远持续下去。

turns.speaker: Ray Cao
turns.en: I think at the end of the day it's a personal choice. It's very much like a personal choice. If you are excited about this, if you want to grow together, yeah, this maybe is a good thing for you. And also depends on the life stage. So some of the people they want to actually getting more family time, I think that's also the right choice, too. But it just depends on your, I would say, your personal choice rather than if the company demands that. I mean, I cannot force my team to working long hours. I don't want them to working long hours. I think it's more about if you are able to deliver, right? If it requires a bit, a longer time to contribute, I think it's okay, but you'll also get rewarded very well too. So what's get in, what's get out. So I think it's, again, I do believe that this is the quality and also the value we're evaluating here as well.
turns.zh: 我认为归根结底，这是一个个人选择的问题。这很像个人选择。如果你对此充满热情，如果你希望与团队共同成长，那么这或许对你来说是件好事。但这也取决于个人所处的人生阶段。比如，有些人希望能有更多家庭时间，我认为这也是正确的选择。不过关键在于，你得根据自身情况来做决定，而不是被公司强制要求。我无法强迫我的团队长时间工作，我也不希望他们这样做。我认为关键在于你是否能胜任工作。如果某项任务需要更长时间才能完成，那也没关系，但你也会因此获得丰厚回报。所谓有舍有得。所以我再次强调，我相信这正是我们所评判的品质和价值所在。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And even though it's hard in the moment, I find that those are the times you remember most and most fondly in your career, when you just go all in, "I'm going to work really hard and do the best possible job I can do." Assuming that doesn't last forever, those end up being the most impactful, helpful to your career. Most proud moments when you're just like, "Look what I had accomplished." And so I'm on the same page. I want to talk about being successful on TikTok as a creator, as a business, as an advertiser. But a couple more questions real quick on how TikTok operates. You mentioned you do OKRs just briefly, is there anything that you've learned about being successful doing OKRs within TikTok? Maybe is there anything different that you all do versus how other companies think about OKRs?
turns.zh: 即便当下很艰难，但我发现这些往往是你职业生涯中最难忘、最珍贵的时刻——当你全力以赴，说：“我要拼尽全力把工作做到最好。”假设这种状态不会永久持续，那么它们最终会成为对你职业生涯最具影响力、最有助益的时刻。那些让你倍感自豪的时刻，比如：“看看我取得了怎样的成就。” 所以我深有同感。我想谈谈在TikTok上如何作为创作者、企业或广告主取得成功。但关于TikTok运营方式，我想再快速问几个问题。你之前简单提到过OKR，请问在TikTok内部使用OKR时，你是否有任何成功经验？与其他公司对OKR的理解相比，你们在TikTok有何独特做法？

turns.speaker: Ray Cao
turns.en: It is definitely a company alignment that we are using OKR as our basically the system to make sure that everybody is working towards the same goal. I think definitely we have a lot of room to improve. So how often do you actually see your team able to go to OKR at the end of a quarter and also putting OKR really two weeks or one week before the beginning of a quarter? I have to say that shame on me. I sometimes delay it a little bit, but I think the goal is always there to using OKR system as our North Star to drive the behavior and also to align. Again, it's very important to align on the OKRs because I can see a lot of times the OKRs are putting in, but they are very siloed and that is not really necessarily helpful for the company want achieving really high growth. So I think it's very important that we know we don't take OKR as a shell, but we take OKR as its core is cross-functional alignment, cross-functional goal silo. So these are the things we're still continuing improving.
turns.zh: 我们确实将OKR作为公司战略工具，确保所有人朝着同一目标努力。我认为我们还有很大的提升空间。那么，你团队通常在季度末才制定OKR吗？或者是否会在季度开始前两周或一周就着手呢？不得不说，我对此深感愧疚。有时我会拖延，但我们的目标始终是将OKR作为核心导航工具，用于行为引导和团队协同。跨部门目标协同至关重要，因为我发现很多时候OKR只是形式化指标，彼此割裂，这对实现公司高速增长毫无助益。因此，我们要确保OKR不仅是表象，更是跨部门协同、目标统一的核心机制。这正是我们持续改进的方向。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Is the way that OKRs work at TikTok, is there an OKR per team and they all kind of trickle up to a company level OKR? Is it less structured that way and teams decide if they want to use OKRs or not? How does that roughly work?
turns.zh: TikTok的OKR运作方式是怎样的？是每个团队各自制定OKR，然后汇总到公司层面吗？这种方式是否更灵活，团队可以自主决定是否使用OKR？具体流程是怎样的？

turns.speaker: Ray Cao
turns.en: The structure is, basically the guidance is, using the key result to evaluating and then you put the steps in between. So that's how at least my team has been using this. I think the things that we can improve is the input and output. So the output is very clear, but what is actually the input sometimes is debatable, sometimes I have to say. And also oftentimes your output is other people's input. Are you able to connect the dots over there, too? Then that's actually the part that requires a lot of, I would say reinforcement alignment. Definitely we're getting better, don't get me wrong. We're totally not perfect, for sure. But I do see there is a lot of, I say momentum, to leveraging the system better. If you know other companies doing this really, really good, please shoot them my way. I would love to learn from them.
turns.zh: 基本上，整个框架是这样的：先用关键成果来评估，然后在中间填充各个步骤。至少我们团队一直是这么用的。我认为我们可以改进的地方在于输入和输出。输出部分很清晰，但输入有时存在争议，有时候我不得不说。而且很多时候，你的输出其实是别人的输入。你能把这些点也串联起来吗？这实际上是需要大量强化和协调的部分。别误会，我们确实在不断进步，但肯定还不够完美。但我确实看到，在更好地利用这个系统方面，有很大的势头。如果你们知道其他公司在这方面做得特别好的，请推荐给我，我很乐意向他们学习。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: One last question here. You do planning, you have OKRs. Just briefly, how often do you all do planning? Is there a yearly plan that you put together and then a quarterly detailed plan?
turns.zh: 最后一个问题：你们做规划，有OKR。简单说一下，你们多久做一次规划？有没有年度计划，再分季度详细规划？

turns.speaker: Ray Cao
turns.en: Yeah, we do have annual planning cycle, but I have to say that our annual planning cycle is the baseline. We often do a lot of iterations in the middle of the year and also on a quarterly basis that we're able to pivoting really nimbly to really catering to the things that we see in the market. Some of the longer term strategy won't change, just like the platform we want to always creating, inspiring and also frictionless and immersive experiences for users. This won't change, but anything into the core of how do we realizing that you're always a consistent experiment over there. I cannot speak for the user product side, but at least from advertising product side that this is always the approach we're taking. And for the go-to-market part, that's also creating a very different behavior for us because oftentimes if we have a solid and kind of a static product roadmap, you can do go-to-market relatively easy, I would say, because everything is planned. But with a environment like that that basically make the go-to-market and also the product feedback loop much more short and faster. (00:48:23): So there's a lot of, I would say, pressure or actually put it nicely, there was a lot of innovative things that on the go-to-market side. Also on the sales side, the company or the teams need to actually do to make sure that we're able to catering for that. But again, this is a teamwork rather than only one side of the work. So far so good, I would say. A lot of things that we've been able to achieve within the past couple of years has been already proven that this approach has been working for us, but not necessarily they're always is perfect already, always room to improve, to make sure that we have more structural approach as well so that the market able to keep the pacing with us. We don't want to overwhelm our advertisers or our users either. So that's also the other part that we need to continue optimizing, too.
turns.zh: 是的，我们有年度规划周期，但我得说我们的年度规划周期只是基准。我们经常在年中和季度进行多次迭代，这样能更灵活地应对市场变化。一些长期战略不会变，比如我们希望始终为用户创造、激发并提供无缝沉浸的体验。这部分不会变，但涉及如何实现的核心部分，你永远在进行持续的实验。我不能代表用户产品团队发言，但至少从广告产品团队来看，这始终是我们的方法。至于市场推广部分，由于环境变化，我们需要更快地调整策略。（00:48:23）：所以有很多创新点，比如在市场推广和销售方面，团队需要确保能跟上节奏。但这毕竟是团队协作，而非单方面努力。到目前为止，我们过去几年取得的成果已经证明这种方法行之有效，但总有改进空间。我们需要更系统的方法，确保市场能跟上我们的步伐，同时又不让广告主和用户感到负担过重。这也是我们需要持续优化的部分。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay. Let's talk about a different topic which is being successful on TikTok. So the way I think about it in my head is, there's how to be successful is just a regular human creator person. How to be successful as a business, trying to just create viral content and then being successful as an advertiser, which I know is where you spend a lot of time. So let me just ask, is there a tip you could share for someone to be successful, say aka go viral on TikTok? I imagine your answer will be just produce something people love and want to share and like. But I guess is there anything that could be tactically useful when you're creating content in TikTok to help you go viral?
turns.zh: 好的。接下来我们来聊聊在TikTok上取得成功的话题。首先，在我看来，有三种成功路径：第一种是作为普通创作者取得成功；第二种是作为企业主，努力创作出爆款内容；第三种是作为广告主，在平台上投放广告。我想问的是，有没有什么实用的技巧能帮助人们在TikTok上走红？我猜你的答案会是创作出人们喜爱、愿意分享和点赞的内容。但我好奇，在创作TikTok内容时，是否有一些战术层面的技巧能助你走红？

turns.speaker: Ray Cao
turns.en: I think if I know that I definitely will already become a very successful creator, I have to say. Our system is very much smarter than I am. I cannot trick the system, but I have seen a couple of good cases. So number one thing is that you have to really be unfiltered. I mean, you don't really need to be perfect on this platform. I mean that's the beauty of it. You can be yourself, you can really share the things that you like. And if you're really master at one thing that you're really, really good at and you want to showcase, this is the platform for you to shine because not necessarily that we are fully saturated and also all algorithm distributing the content in a very different way. Some of the other platforms they are, I would say like a people-based or friend-based. (00:50:32): I think for us it's purely based on actually you're creating something that everybody want to see. So let's see if we can distribute it more. So I think continuously to bring new content to this platform and testing and finding your own competitive edge going to be very important as a successful creator. And most of our creators have been doing that. And I can see some of our biggest TikTok stars, they're literally practicing this every single day. And I do think that creativity and that part of, I would say, getting the nuances is the key part that to be more successful on the T TikTok community. (00:51:11): And the second thing is it's including also for brands as well, because I consider brands as our creator as well. They really need to embrace the culture and the community here to really listen and understand what are the user behaviors on the platform to understand what do they like to see. And also the messages or the presence could be very different from your other media channels, or as a creator, it could be very different from your other, I would say, platforms. (00:51:40): So that's the other thing that it's going to be challenging because for them to shift in the mindset. But I do think that definitely was trial. Some of the, I would say, our early adopters has already been proven that when you do embrace the culture here, you're able to acquire a ton of different kind of a user or the audience to your channel and you can show a different side of yourself as well. So yeah, I've been trying to do that. I have not really finding my competitive edge I have to say, but I'll keep trying.
turns.zh: 我觉得如果我知道的话，我肯定早就已经成为非常成功的创作者了。说实话，我们的系统比我聪明得多。我没法糊弄它，但我确实见过几个成功的案例。首先，你必须保持真实。这里不需要完美，平台的美妙之处就在于，你可以做自己，分享你喜欢的东西。如果你精通某项技能，并且想展示出来，TikTok就是你大放异彩的舞台，因为我们的平台并不饱和，算法分发内容的方式也与其他平台不同。其他平台可能更侧重于人际关系或好友关系。而TikTok完全基于用户真正想看的内容。关键在于持续为平台输送新内容，测试并找到自己的竞争优势。这对成功的创作者来说至关重要，我们平台上的大多数创作者都在这么做。我能看到一些顶级TikTok明星每天都在践行这一点。创造力和理解平台细微之处的能力，是在TikTok社区取得成功的关键。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Is there an example you could share of someone that has done that really well, either be really authentic and also embrace the community of a business specifically that has done this really well and has taken off not as an advertiser?
turns.zh: 还有第二点，对品牌来说同样适用，因为我也把品牌视为创作者。他们需要融入这里的文化和社区，倾听并理解用户行为，了解他们喜欢看什么。品牌在TikTok上的呈现方式，可能与其他媒体渠道或其他平台截然不同。这对他们来说是个挑战，但我相信已经有成功案例。一些早期入局者证明，只要拥抱这里的文化，就能吸引大量用户，并展现出不同的一面。我一直在努力，但不得不说还没找到自己的竞争优势，但我会继续尝试。

turns.speaker: Ray Cao
turns.en: There was one creator I remember called Sheba. She's a singer and she is able to caught my eyes because she was able to basically rap and also during some of the songs cover in a very different way because she's a minority and she was able to basically using her minority identity as actually everybody was thinking, "I'm supposed to be doing Bollywood music, but actually, you know what I'm not. I'm doing a lot of very just hip hop and also the music that people may think like I'm not good at." (00:52:59): So it is pretty fun to watch that kind of a comparison or the contrast between a creator and also she's able to put a lot of original music on the platform to really inspire more people to do the same thing. There's another music, I would say TikTok creator. So he was pretty big on the other platforms, but the total approach from him is he's basically changing the lyrics, make it very relatable as a personal life. Because for example, he can totally change the lyrics from a old Backstreet Boys song or Nsync song to make it related with his daily communication with his wife. Make it really relatable and fun. So these are the things I think is very unique to us. If you are able to test and find something new like that, you're able to find a new batch of audience and even go viral on the platform.
turns.zh: 有一位我印象深刻的创作者叫谢芭。她是一名歌手，能吸引我的地方在于，她既能说唱，还能用非常独特的方式翻唱一些歌曲。作为少数族裔，她能够利用自己的身份特质，打破人们对她"应该做宝莱坞音乐"的刻板印象，实际上，她创作了很多嘻哈风格的音乐，甚至是那些人们认为她不擅长的音乐类型。（00:52:59）观察这种创作者之间的对比或反差非常有趣，她还能够在平台上发布大量原创音乐，激励更多人效仿。还有一位音乐创作者，我觉得他在TikTok上很火，但他的整体策略是通过改编歌词，让歌曲更贴近个人生活。比如，他能把后街男孩或NSYNC的旧歌歌词改编成与自己和妻子日常交流相关的主题，既接地气又有趣。这就是我认为TikTok独具特色的地方。如果你能尝试创新，就能吸引新观众，甚至在平台上走红。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: So then switching to the advertising network, a lot of listeners here are thinking about, I imagine, advertising on TikTok. There's kind of classically been Facebook and Google are the two places to do run paid ads. Paid ads are a huge growth driver for tons of companies. It's one of the easiest you could say, or one of the most traditional way to grow. TikTok obviously is emerging and has already emerged as one of the newer advertising networks. So there's a lot of people thinking about how do I succeed as an advertiser on TikTok. So what advice do you have for people? One, who's it best for? I imagine TikTok isn't the best place to advertise for every sort of business. So what sort of businesses are best aligned to be successful on TikTok? And then just what advice can you share to do well as an advertiser on TikTok?
turns.zh: 接下来谈谈广告投放网络。我猜很多听众都在考虑在TikTok上投放广告。传统上，Facebook和Google是投放付费广告的两个主要平台。付费广告是许多公司增长的重要驱动力，甚至可以说是最直接、最传统的增长方式。显然，TikTok正逐渐崛起，并已成为新兴的广告平台。因此，许多人都在思考如何在TikTok上成功投放广告。您对此有什么建议吗？首先，TikTok最适合哪些类型的企业？我觉得并非所有行业都适合在TikTok上投放广告。那么哪些行业最适合在TikTok上取得成功呢？最后，您能给出哪些在TikTok上投放广告的实用建议？

turns.speaker: Ray Cao
turns.en: Yeah, I see a lot of really different type of advertisers already find their success on the platform. One thing that they actually can do that is really due to a couple of things that they're doing. Number one is, like I said, they're embracing this platform. They actually do a lot of things is TikTok first. I have a couple of advertisers. They have actually creating their own internal creative team just dedicated for TikTok. So they actually produce a ton of creative every single day to actually test and learn to understand the platform and understand the community they are engaging with. So I would say leaning in is the first part. It's harder, but it is not that hard. As long as you try it, you'll feel that every single day is getting easier. And also we make a lot of tools to make things easier for them as well. Like creative, we have also a lot of resources on the platform, the creative hub and also we have creative analytics to help you. So these are the things that we're able to basically help the advertiser to leaning in more. (00:55:42): The other angle to leaning in more is test and learn. A lot of times that people don't know how to really run ads on this platform. Google is very much search, like search fronts. They are really leading on the intent graph. And Meta is really on the people graph they're making. I mean TikTok is the content graph. It's very different, I would say machine compared to the other two. And it requires different way to optimizing and to leveraging the tools we have. So if you're applying the same logic from Meta or Google into TikTok, not necessarily you'll be able to see a great success, I have to say. (00:56:27): So you have to really get to the detail and to learn how you're operating this platform at the very beginning. Of course, like I said, we're trying to make things as simple as possible because we strongly believe that an advertiser's job is to taking care of their own business and our job is to service them. So we definitely make things a bit easier and along the way, but still it's a little bit learning for advertisers to change their mindset when they engage with us the first time. And I can see that again, for example, last Q4, I can see a lot of advertisers taking this approach to really listen to us and understanding what is our best practices. They actually see a very successful Q4 on the platform. So I do think that if you want to do more, just do more test and learn with us and to really understand the impact from TikTok.
turns.zh:
是的，我看到很多不同类型的广告主已经在该平台上取得了成功。他们成功的关键在于他们所采取的几项策略。首先，他们真正拥抱了这个平台。他们很多工作都是以TikTok为先导的。我接触过一些广告主，他们甚至专门为TikTok组建了内部创意团队。因此，他们每天都会创作大量创意内容，用于测试和了解平台特性及用户群体。所以我认为主动投入是关键。尽管这并不容易，但只要坚持尝试，每一天都会变得越来越顺手。同时，我们也提供了诸多工具来助力广告主：比如创意资源库、创意分析工具等。这些举措有助于广告主更深入地融入平台。

（00:55:42）：在深入探索平台的过程中，测试与学习同样重要。很多广告主不清楚如何在TikTok上有效投放广告。谷歌主打搜索，专注于用户意图分析；Meta则专注于社交图谱；而TikTok则以内容图谱为核心，与前两者相比有本质差异。这就要求我们采用不同策略优化投放效果，充分利用平台工具。如果将Meta或谷歌的投放逻辑直接套用到TikTok上，效果未必理想。

（00:56:27）：因此，广告主需要从一开始就深入了解平台运作机制。当然，我们致力于让平台操作尽可能简单化，因为我们坚信广告主的核心职责是专注业务发展，而我们的任务是提供优质服务。因此，我们不断优化平台体验，但在初期合作中，广告主仍需转变思维模式。例如，去年第四季度，我观察到许多广告主通过积极倾听我们的建议，掌握最佳实践，最终在TikTok上取得了显著成果。因此，我认为若想深挖潜力，关键在于持续测试与学习，深入理解TikTok的运营逻辑。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Just to understand this point about versus Instagram, I think a lot of people probably run on them on both platforms and try to see which one's working better. Your point is the same content won't work as well on one versus the other. So just so people understand what the main difference there is. I know you talk about there's the friend graph versus TikTok just spreads it all over and anyone can see it. You don't have to be friends and it's really good at getting content out. So what is it that you would do differently if you're making an ad video for Instagram versus TikTok?
turns.zh: 关于与Instagram的对比，我想很多人可能同时在两个平台上投放广告，试图判断哪个效果更好。您的核心观点是，相同的内容在不同平台效果差异巨大。能否请您为大家解析两者的主要区别？我知道您提到了Instagram的社交图谱，而TikTok则将内容广泛分发，任何用户都能看到，无需加好友，这对内容传播非常有利。那么，如果要为Instagram和TikTok制作广告视频，您会采取哪些不同的策略？

turns.speaker: Ray Cao
turns.en: I think the TikTok video, it's more about the backend settings, right? So how often do you actually changing creatives? I think for us it is actually pretty... you want to actually test more creatives on this platform and see which one is actually working. And then we also have really detailed guidance on how do you set up your campaign structure to make sure that you're able to be more successful on the platform. So these are, I would say, the basic hydrangeas we talked about. You can see these guidance are very different from what Meta has today or even Google has today because we're just basically different platforms. And oftentimes you can also hear that we requires a bit more real time react on the platform due to some of the trends we have seen. (00:58:30): So that is the part I feel like if advertiser wants to engage more with really the sales team and they're able to provide more guidance to you and you're able to see more success there. But a lot of things will be counterintuitive I would say, because the intuitive you have learned is coming from the other platforms, but technically we're not. So a lot of things that, "Oh, this doesn't make sense to me, but why don't you try it?" And we make actually that really easy because we are sharing a lot of, I would say added credit to intensify incentivizing our advertisers to try it at the end of the day that hopefully they can see the result is proven itself.
turns.zh: 我觉得TikTok的视频更多的是关于后台设置的，对吧？那么你们实际更换创意的频率有多高呢？我觉得对我们来说，实际上是相当……你希望在这个平台上测试更多的创意，看看哪一个真正有效。然后我们还有非常详细的指导，告诉你如何设置你的广告活动结构，确保你在平台上能取得更大的成功。所以这些，我想可以说是我们所谈到的基本要素。你可以看到这些指导与Meta或者Google目前的做法非常不同，因为我们毕竟是不同的平台。很多时候你也会听到，我们需要在平台上更实时地做出反应，因为我们看到了一些趋势。（00:58:30）：所以这就是我觉得，如果广告商想与销售团队有更多互动，他们能够为你提供更多指导，而你也能够看到更大的成功。但很多事情会是违背直觉的，我会说，你学到的直觉来自其他平台，但技术层面我们不一样。所以很多事情，比如“哦，这对我来说没意义，但你为什么不试试呢？” 而我们实际上让这变得非常容易，因为我们分享了很多信息，我会说增加激励措施，让我们的广告商最终能够看到结果的价值。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Got it. I think that's such an interesting point, this idea of testing more, which basically you're saying with Instagram certain people will see it and that's not going to be shown tons of random people. So you basically have one shot at getting this in front of the Instagram crowd versus TikTok just tries it, this explore and exploit kind of approach is like, we'll just keep trying stuff until something sticks.
turns.zh: 明白了。我觉得这是一个非常有趣的观点，这个测试更多的想法，基本上你是在说Instagram上某些人会看到它，而不会被展示给大量随机的人。所以你基本上只有一次机会让Instagram的用户看到你的内容，而TikTok只是尝试这种探索和利用的方法，就像我们会不断尝试，直到找到有效的方法。

turns.speaker: Ray Cao
turns.en: Yeah, I think exactly like that 100%. I think a lot of times that I think advertising, especially when digital advertising becomes a thing, so we kind of think everything can be calculated because you have the data, but the beauty of advertising is never like that. The core value advertising is to tell people don't know you exist and tell them that what you're doing for them and then creating these demand, right? Discovery is the core of advertising to me because I was never expecting my wife telling me that what she going to buy when she walk into a shopping mall, if I know that I'll stop her already. She oftentimes that get out something different. So this is not planned. I think that's literally one of the behavior I would love to emphasize more is you want to be open up your door to more consumer. (01:00:26): Because we are a digital version of word-of-mouth, I always compare us to that because it is the way that how the digital era becomes more human because it is actually helping user to discover new things, just like what they used to do. There's a new place in a certain area, you just go explore. It is just like that. So I think that's the reason why I think at the very beginning, continue doing this kind of open-minded testing with us will be a very good approach to get some early learning and eventually that you can refine your approach. But at the beginning I would highly recommend that just be open up and also take some risks with us together and we're able to show you how much we can actually benefit in the business.
turns.zh:
是的，我完全同意这一点。我觉得很多时候，特别是当数字广告成为一种趋势后，我们会觉得一切都可以被量化，因为你有数据，但广告的核心价值从来不是这样的。广告的核心价值是告诉那些不知道你存在的人，并告诉他们你为他们做了什么，然后创造需求，对吧？对我来说，发现是广告的核心，因为我从未预料到我的妻子会在进入商场时告诉我她要买什么，如果我知道的话，我早就拦住她了。她经常会买到不同的东西。这不是计划好的。我认为这正是我想强调的核心价值之一，就是你要向更多的消费者敞开大门。
（01:00:26）：因为我们是数字版的口碑传播，我总是拿这个来比较，因为这正是数字时代变得更人性化的方式，因为它实际上是在帮助用户发现新事物，就像他们过去做的那样。在某个地区有一个新地方，你就去探索。就是这样。所以我认为这就是为什么我认为一开始就和我们一起进行这种开放测试将是一个很好的方法，可以获得一些早期学习，最终你可以优化你的方法。但一开始我强烈建议你保持开放心态，和我们一起冒些风险，我们能够向你展示我们能为你的业务带来多大的好处。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Awesome. And on that point, that was the other piece of advice you shared is pay attention to the trends so that you can connect your ad to things that people are already laughing at or finding really interesting. I feel like Duolingo is incredible at this. Their videos are hilarious and I think they're all just organic videos and a lot of them connected trends that are-
turns.zh: 太棒了。说到这点，你之前分享的另一个建议就是要关注热点趋势，这样你的广告才能紧跟人们正在热议或感兴趣的话题。我觉得Duolingo在这方面做得特别棒。他们的视频超级搞笑，而且看起来都是自然生成的内容，很多视频都紧扣了当时的热点趋势——

turns.speaker: Ray Cao
turns.en: Yeah. It's funny you brought up Duolingo because I'm actually now become a heavy user of Duolingo myself because-
turns.zh: 是啊，你提到Duolingo这点挺有意思的，我现在自己也成了Duolingo的重度用户，因为——

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Me, too.
turns.zh: 我也是。

turns.en: I watched the video on the TikTok. I think just basically kids just randomly learn a different language and make a lot of mistakes and it's really funny. And then I just download the app because I didn't know. I've been using Duolingo for the past 40 days as a New Year resolution. I'm convincing myself to learn Japanese.
turns.zh: 我在TikTok上看了那个视频。我觉得基本上就是孩子们随意学习不同语言，犯很多错误，特别搞笑。然后我下载了这个应用，因为之前不了解。我把学习日语当作新年决心，已经坚持40天了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Wow, 40-day streak?
turns.zh: 哇，坚持40天了？

turns.speaker: Ray Cao
turns.en: Yeah.

turns.en: Amazing. I'm at 25 days.

turns.zh: 你现在是红宝石级别还是翡翠级别？

turns.en: Emerald, right now.

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Just to close the thread on this, so you're talking about one of the benefits of TikTok ads is awareness-building basically more top of funnel. I know you also focus a lot on taking action, not just brand awareness. There's also a lot of, so maybe talk a bit about that, just like that's also a big part of advertising and TikTok.
turns.zh: 总结一下，关于TikTok广告的好处之一就是提高品牌知名度，属于顶部漏斗阶段。我知道你也非常关注转化，而不只是品牌认知。还有很多方面，可能可以多讲讲这部分，毕竟这也是广告和TikTok的重要组成部分。

turns.speaker: Ray Cao
turns.en: Yeah, I think the beauty of word-of-mouth is actually that word-of-mouth leads to actions. So I think TikTok, we oftentimes people are thinking that, oh, TikTok is really good for building awareness, building upper funnel or some of the discovery funnel. But I really want to say that we want to prove, and also we already proved that from the studies we have seen from third parties that we're driving actions at the same time, and this is literally the ambition we're trying to really talk to out of the advertisers, especially on the commerce front, that shopping and TikTok shop and shop ads. It is actually the proven points that we see. And also, this is not necessarily coming off of our illusion, right, because we see there was a biggest trend on TikTok is "TikTok made me buy it." We have billion level views on that. (01:03:27): It's continue growing and this literally inspire us to do this product. Like I said, one of the very important things here is we drive our product by listening to our user and see the behavior from them and we see the behavior and now we're trying to capture that and provide the best service to our user and also help advertisers to reshaping their product. So I do think that this year people will see us more as a full funnel solution platform rather than only building the brands because we want actually impacting on full funnel for our advertisers. Again, driving their business result is more important to us.
turns.zh: 是的，我觉得口碑传播的美妙之处在于它能直接促成行动。所以我觉得TikTok，我们经常会觉得，哦，TikTok真的很适合建立知名度，属于顶部漏斗或发现阶段。但我真的想说，我们想证明，也确实从第三方研究中看到，我们同时在推动转化，这也是我们试图向广告主传达的愿景，尤其是在电商领域，购物和TikTok商店及购物广告。这确实是我们看到的经证实的点。另外，这也不一定是我们的幻想，对吧，因为我们看到TikTok上最大的趋势是“TikTok让我买了它”。这个视频的播放量达到了数十亿次。（01:03:27）：它还在持续增长，这真的激励我们开发这个产品。就像我说的，这里最重要的一点是，我们通过倾听用户需求来推动产品发展，看他们的行为，现在我们正努力捕捉这些行为，为用户提供最佳服务，同时帮助广告主重塑他们的产品。所以我确实认为今年，人们会更多地把我们视为一个全漏斗解决方案平台，而不仅仅是品牌建设，因为我们真正想为广告主带来全漏斗影响。再次强调，提升他们的业务成果对我们来说更重要。

How much budget should they allot to just explore this as a growth channel for them?
turns.zh: 假设一家初创公司正考虑在TikTok上投放广告，或许他们之前已经尝试过谷歌广告和Facebook广告。您建议他们如何规划投放策略，以评估这是否适合他们的业务？需要投入多少时间？投放多少广告？又该拨出多少预算来探索TikTok作为增长渠道的潜力？

turns.speaker: Ray Cao
turns.en: I would say at the very beginning, the investment will be coming from their leaning into creating a business account with us. So this is actually how you're engaging with your community. But even before that, I think just do some research on a platform and be the user as a TikTok to really experiencing it and see the differences. And then you are thinking about how can you actually connecting your behavior or your desired behavior coming from a user with your business and then you're creating content around it. And that's the moment I think this first step is creating your business presence on the TikTok.
turns.zh: 我认为首先，投资将源于他们倾向于在我们平台上创建企业账号。这实际上是与社区互动的方式。但在此之前，我建议他们先对平台进行深入研究，以用户身份体验TikTok，感受其差异。然后，思考如何将用户的行为或期望与业务需求相结合，并围绕这些内容进行创作。在我看来，第一步就是在TikTok上建立企业形象。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And the idea there is just an organic account you create, let's say Lenny's Podcast, which I actually have... my Lenny's Podcast is on TikTok, so we can use that as an example maybe. turns.zh: 这里提到的可能是创建一个自然成长的账号，比如我自己的“Lenny's Podcast”账号。您是说先在TikTok上创建免费的企业账号，发布视频，感受一下效果如何？

turns.en: Yeah. Just see how it feels, right? So maybe some of the videos you don't get any views and some of the videos, you get more views. At the end of the day you can test some of the advertising products, drive those awareness and see if it's actually driving impact for you. And then you have to do more maybe testing with us or AB testing or geo-splitting testing eventually, depends on how big the investment is. You can see there is actually a directional impact on your business and also we are giving you reporting and insights on how you're doing on the platform, so you can optimize in towards that. (01:05:50): But obviously very important part is trying to get a feeling of the platform by creating your organic presence and then try to launch the ads account to make sure that you're able to drive more traffic to your desired destination or to a desired actions that you want user to take and continue refining that. Along the way, there are a lot of things that you're going to learn. For example, how can you leverage in automation solutions on the platform and how can leveraging some of the, I would say, creator trends you detected on the platform and also some of the tools that we're creating to help you to generating those scripts. (01:06:24): So these are all the things that you can learn from the platform. In terms of time investment, I think at the beginning of the month, definitely it's going to be, I hope it'll be a little bit more intense of learning so that you're able to get a rhythm in there and along the way that as long as gets become more automated and also get more understanding towards the business, you're able to actually creating, I would say, more relevant content for the platforms by leveraging our creators or by leveraging some of your own, I would say, resources from their third party, for example. So I think, yeah, it takes a little bit a learning curve, but I do think that the result will surprise you.
turns.zh: 是的，先感受一下氛围。有些视频可能无人观看，有些则获得较高播放量。最后，可以测试一些广告产品，提升品牌知名度，并观察其对业务的影响。后续可能需要进行A/B测试或地理分割测试，具体取决于投资规模。通过平台提供的数据分析和洞察，您可以持续优化策略。（01:05:50）但关键在于通过自然增长的账号探索平台，之后再启动广告账户，确保流量能准确导向目标页面或促成用户行动，并持续优化策略。过程中，您会学到很多东西，比如如何利用平台的自动化解决方案，如何洞察平台上的创作者趋势，以及如何借助我们的工具生成优质内容。（01:06:24）这些都是从平台中获取的宝贵经验。时间投入方面，初期需要集中精力学习，确保形成节奏。随着流程自动化和业务理解加深，您将能够利用我们的创作者资源或第三方工具，为平台创作更具针对性的内容。虽然有学习曲线，但成果必将超出您的预期。

turns.en: I think oftentimes we'll say a month minimum to run ads because I think it's actually a learning curve for advertisers to really get into understanding the behavior and the platform.

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And how many ads would you suggest, and I know there's not a rule of thumb, but just how many ads would you suggest they try to run in that month, to give you a real sense of this could work or no?
turns.zh: 那你建议投放多少广告呢？虽然没有一个标准答案，但你能不能给个大概的建议，比如一个月至少尝试投放多少广告，让我们更清楚这样做是否有效？

turns.speaker: Ray Cao
turns.en: The more, the better. I would say at least 10 different ad creatives will be ideal per week and the more the better.
turns.zh: 越多越好。我建议每周至少尝试10种不同的广告创意，这样效果最佳。

turns.en: 10 per week. Oh, wow. Okay. So 40 potentially.
turns.zh: 每周10种。哇，好的！那一个月可能就是40种。

turns.en: Yeah, 10 per week. We have CapCut as a tool. I created my anniversary video for my wife by using that tool. Don't tell her one-minute now everybody knows, but she thinks that-
turns.zh: 对，每周10种。另外，我想说我们可以看到，有些人会说"我没有那么多资源"，但其实很简单，这只是一个工具。我们有CapCut这个工具。我用它为妻子制作了周年视频。别告诉她哦，免得大家都知道了，但她以为——

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: She might not listen all the way this long to the end of this episode.
turns.zh: 她可能听不到这期节目的结尾。

turns.speaker: Ray Cao
turns.en: She thinks it takes a lot of time. Literally the production is amazing. We are creating that tool specifically for our creator and also for our monetizer and the user in general. So you're able to do a lot of, I would say, automated and customized way in the app so you're able to generate those content on your fingertips. So it will be a really good help for advertisers that want to be more self-service. On the other hand, we also have third parties, certified TikTok service providers on the creative side to help you as well. So depends on the level of how advertiser you are.
turns.zh: 她觉得这太费时间了。实际上制作效果很棒。我们专门为创作者、变现者和普通用户开发了这个工具。你可以在应用中以自动化和个性化的方式快速生成内容。这对希望更自主操作的广告主来说是个很好的帮助。另一方面，我们也有经过认证的TikTok服务商，可以提供创意方面的支持。具体取决于广告主的水平。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Is there a most common mistake people make when they try this out where you're just often being like, "You fool, here's what you did wrong?" Is there something in there that's just like, "Just don't do this thing because a lot of people make this mistake and then they fail on TikTok?"
turns.zh: 人们在尝试时最常犯的错误是什么？你有没有那种想说，"你个笨蛋，你做错了什么？"的时刻？有没有什么经验可以分享，比如"别这么做，因为很多人都犯了这个错误，然后在TikTok上失败了"？

turns.speaker: Ray Cao
turns.en: Yeah, the first one is I can see a lot of advertiser instantly they want to do remarketing or they want to do a very small niche targeting on the platform because you're limiting yourself. Like I said, it is more about getting to the rhythm to understand more about platform. So a broader targeting approach is actually recommended at the very early stage and most of advertisers are already doing that today because previously I can see for the first two years in the business, especially when we acquire new advertisers, oftentimes they get on the platform, say, "Hey, I want to do this and that. I want to really refine my targeting, et cetera." And then we just recommend, "Hey, why don't we do this comparison? You have a campaign set up like this going on, but this is our recommendation and you can see the difference." And literally most of them, they'll see a very big difference over there on it.
turns.zh: 是的，第一个常见错误是很多广告主一上来就想做再营销，或者在平台上做非常狭窄的定向投放，这样其实是在自我设限。我之前说过，关键是先掌握平台的节奏，了解更多平台机制。所以在初期阶段，建议采用更广泛的定向策略。如今大多数广告主已经在这么做了。回想前两年的经验，尤其是新客户接入时，他们经常上来就想"我要做这个做那个，我要精细化定向"，然后我们会建议他们"不如先对比一下吧，你现在正在运行的campaign是这样的，但我们推荐你试试这个，你会看到效果差别很大"。结果大多数人都能明显感受到效果提升。
